newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends down on LME losses.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends down on LME losses.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down on Wednesday due to overnight losses on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active February 1997 contract ended at an intra-day low of 18,980 yuan ($2,287) per tonne, down 270 yuan. It opened at 19,100 and hit a high of 19,150.
November fell 140 to 18,840 yuan per tonne, December 250 to 18,860, January 220 to 18,990, March 230 to 19,020, April 190 to 19,050 and May 150 to 19,070.
Combined volume rose to 43,710 tonnes from 15,150.
Copper opened lower and fell before most contracts closed near their intra-day lows.
Traders said that LME losses triggered speculative selling and that copper would test the 18,500-yuan level if it could not hold the 19,000-yuan level in the short term.
"LME losses were the key reason for today's falls but the low price of spot copper was also negative for investors," one trader said.
The price of spot copper was around 19,000-19,300 yuan.
But traders said sharp further falls were unlikely in the absence of market-moving news.

"Despite heavy pressure from spot copper, there was no panic selling, which indicated that most investors were unsure of the market trend," a second trader said. Analysts said that falls are more likely than rises in the next few days.
Aluminium ended down. November fell 100 to 13,400 yuan per tonne, December 100 to 13,220 and January 30 to 13,250.
Combined volume rose to 990 tonnes from 570.
